tweet_text: 🧠 Binary search isn’t magic. Most developers fail because they ignore its rules. Let’s fix that 👇
Binary search ONLY works when the array is sorted, boundaries are correct, and mid is calculated safely.
Binary search rewards discipline, not tricks. Master it once and reuse it forever. 📌 #DSA #Algorithms
🧠 Most bugs hide at the edges, not the middle.
Always test: null, empty, first, last, min, max. Edge cases expose broken assumptions.
If you don’t test boundaries, production will. ⚠️ #DSA #ProblemSolving
⚠️ `volatile` in Java feels safe. It isn’t.
It guarantees visibility ❌ atomicity. `count++` is still broken.
Use AtomicInteger, synchronized, or locks for correctness. Concurrency bugs fail quietly. #Java #Concurrency
☕ Immutable objects make concurrent code boring — and that’s good.
No setters. Final fields. Defensive copies. Less state, fewer bugs.
Prefer immutability by default. Opt out only when needed. #Java #CleanCode
🏗 Most production outages aren’t code bugs. They’re observability failures.
If logs can’t answer: which request, which user, which service — they’re broken.
Structured logs with context and trace IDs save hours of debugging. 📌 #SystemDesign #Architecture
🧼 If a class has more than one reason to change, a bug is already waiting.
Single Responsibility Principle isn’t theory. It keeps code testable and sane.
Clean code scales better than clever code. #CleanCode #SoftwareEngineering
💼 Interviews aren’t about perfect code.
They test how you think, communicate, and reason about trade-offs.
Explain your decisions, not just your solution. That’s how you stand out. #Jobs #Interviews
🧠 Recursion without memoization wastes computation.
If subproblems repeat, cache results. That’s dynamic programming.
DP turns exponential nightmares into linear solutions. #DSA #ProblemSolving
☕ Enum-based Singleton in Java is thread-safe, serialization-safe, and simple. Avoid classic singleton pitfalls. #Java #DesignPatterns
🧠 HashMaps give O(1) on average — not guaranteed. Bad hashing leads to bad performance. #DSA #Programming
🧼 Methods should do ONE thing. Long methods hide logic, increase bugs, and complicate testing. #CleanCode #SoftwareDesign
🏗 Factory pattern centralizes object creation, reduces coupling, and improves testability. Stop scattering constructors. #SystemDesign #CleanCode
☕ Optional forces explicit handling of absence. Fewer NullPointerExceptions, clearer APIs. #Java #CleanCode
🧠 Graphs model real systems: networks, maps, dependencies.
BFS, DFS, Dijkstra — choosing the right algorithm matters more than memorizing them.
Understand graph types and representations to solve real problems. #DSA #SoftwareEngineering
🧼 Magic numbers hide intent. Meaningful constants improve readability and prevent errors. #CleanCode #ProgrammingTips

🧠 Most DSA mistakes aren’t algorithmic. They’re assumptions. Let’s talk about the most common one 👇
Developers assume input is clean, sorted, or non-empty. Reality disagrees.
Always validate assumptions before optimizing logic. That’s senior-level problem solving. #DSA #ProblemSolving
⚠️ Concurrency bugs don’t crash your app.
They corrupt data slowly, silently, and randomly.
If a bug disappears under debugging, suspect race conditions. #Java #Concurrency
🧼 If code needs comments to explain *what* it does, rewrite it. Comments should explain *why*, not *what*. #CleanCode

☕ Java performance issues are often memory issues.
Leaky references keep objects alive longer than expected.
Understand GC roots before blaming the JVM. #Java #Performance
🏗 Systems don’t fail at small scale.
They fail when assumptions break under load.
Design for failure, not perfection. #SystemDesign #Architecture

• scale
